summary: Seek bounded message pages through body-free temporal selectors

replay.detail: Opening an older database backfills local message selector headers from current message projections and retained canonical claims in short, resumable chunks before readers are served. Starting a backfill invalidates existing page cuts. No authoritative claim replay or body-copy inventory is introduced; ordinary pages fold only selected message bodies.

schema.detail: Adds the local-only projection local_client_message_selectors_v1: one header/pending table with fourteen ordered eligibility, reminder and retirement indexes plus one partial pending-row index, six source-change triggers, a completed-cut metadata marker and a resumable backfill progress marker. Selectors retain only recipient, sender, canonical order, closed/reminder eligibility and cut intervals, never message bodies. Writes maintain changed selectors in their transaction; body-only changes add no selector version. In isolated two-order 128-send/128-close bursts through the real append path, selector maintenance changed send p95 by -0.094 and +0.996 ms and close p95 by +1.002 and +0.700 ms, with 50.5% additional send WAL and 75.1% additional close WAL. The existing cursor epoch table and its deletion/update/repair triggers remain. Earlier body version tables and their maintenance triggers are removed idempotently. The projection adds no subject, resource or claim vocabulary, so the schema registry digest, replication compatibility digest, authoritative claims and claim formats are unchanged; docs/st3/schema.md documents the local table.

rules.detail: Checkpoint rules, the schema registry digest and shared projection digests are unchanged. Deletion or repair that destroys a retained message cut, or a selector backfill start, invalidates that traversal instead of returning a partial successful page.

compatibility.detail: Message JSON, recipient/actor filters, ordering, reminder selection and snapshot-consistent traversal are preserved. Fresh pages honor current desired-projection deletion: retained intent.desired claims do not restore removed message fields or recipient membership. Continuations require bounded server-issued metadata that binds the exact store cut, snapshot, filters, limit, position and expiry. Tampered, expired, evicted, restarted or deletion-invalidated cursors return HTTP 410/page-cursor-expired and require restarting pagination. Delivery presence remains live on each page while delivery age retains the first request time.

downtime.detail: Initial selector backfill runs at startup in bounded write transactions that record their progress, so an interrupted backfill resumes rather than restarting, and message pages are refused until it completes. On a fresh temporary copy of a checkpointed 118,390-claim, 9,712-message, 1.65-GiB database, the startup backfill took 4.673 s in 610 transactions; the longest transaction, including commit, took 18.579 ms. Store open including all startup work took 11.377 s, and a populated reopen took 17.490 ms with no backfill transaction. These are API-only Store measurements, not live-daemon restart-to-API or rollout downtime proofs.

manual.detail: No manual migration, identity change or claim-log maintenance is required. Clients restart pagination on page-cursor-expired.

recovery.detail: Binary swap-back cannot restore issued in-memory cursor metadata; clients restart traversals. The authoritative claim log remains intact and older claim-based readers continue to work. A runtime that reintroduces the removed local body version store must recreate and seed it from claims.
